title: Picross 3D: Round 2
subtitle: An object hidden in a block
summary: Picross 3D: Round 2 is HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 3DS puzzle game about revealing objects inside three-dimensional arrangements of cubes. Numbers along rows and columns describe which parts should remain, while the player removes or colours blocks to uncover the model. The sequel introduces two colours with different roles, expanding the deductions available from a clue. Each finished puzzle turns a numerical plan into a recognisable little object. body: Picross 3D: Round 2 is HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 3DS puzzle game about revealing objects inside three-dimensional arrangements of cubes. Numbers along rows and columns describe which parts should remain, while the player removes or colours blocks to uncover the model. The sequel introduces two colours with different roles, expanding the deductions available from a clue. Each finished puzzle turns a numerical plan into a recognisable little object. The process feels like careful sculpting, except that the intended form is already encoded in information placed around its surface.

Blue blocks represent straight square pieces, while orange blocks can become curved or cut-out parts of the completed model. A row can contain both kinds, requiring the player to interpret their relationship rather than only a total. Incorrect removal or colouring incurs a penalty, while flags allow uncertain ideas to be marked before committing. The distinction gives a familiar grid puzzle another dimension of reasoning. A cube may be needed in the final object, but knowing that is only part of the answer when its colour determines the shape it will become.

Each puzzle offers three difficulty settings, allowing its challenge to be adjusted while retaining the same small act of discovery. Rows known to contain no required blocks can be cleared quickly, leaving attention for the clues that still need interpretation. More than 370 puzzles provide a substantial collection of finished models, with additional Nintendo-themed ones available through compatible amiibo. The game makes that accumulation appealing through the difference between the starting mass and the final object. A collection grows because the player has patiently reasoned each little shape out of hiding.
